_comment: Provider registry and pinned price table. Prices are NOT fetchable at runtime: the endpoints return no pricing, so every figure here is transcribed by hand from the provider's published page, with that URL and the retrieval date recorded. Every receipt carries this file's version and sha256.
_rule: A model with no entry here cannot be metered and MUST NOT appear in the leaderboard. usd_list is 'what this would cost anyone' at published list price -- it is NOT what we paid. A call served by a free tier still reports the published list price, and the actual spend of zero is a separate fact.

opencode.status: BLOCKED — GATE 0, 7 Sep: free tier is client-only and the API refuses it; paid models report an empty balance

groq.status: ACTIVE — 3 model(s) selected: open-weight only, R14 reviewers excluded
groq.price_origin: fetched from the provider /models endpoint, then pinned

openrouter.status: ACTIVE — 4 PAID model(s) selected: open-weight only, R14 reviewers excluded. All four smoke-tested against the real key; each answered and returned token usage.
openrouter.price_origin: fetched from https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models on 2026-09-09, then pinned by hand
openrouter._why_not_the_free_tier: ⚠️ The three ':free' entries below are LISTED but NOT selected, and the entries are kept so that decision is visible rather than silent. Two reasons. The builder's: a benchmark of models nobody pays for is not the question being asked. The methodological one: a free endpoint's serving configuration -- quantisation, context truncation, routing to a different deployment -- cannot be verified from outside, so the model id may not identify what actually ran. That is a possibility rather than a measured fact, and it is enough to prefer the paid route when the paid route costs a fifth of a cent per run.
openrouter._cost_reality: Measured from the 15 receipts already published: a run costs between $0.0009 and $0.0108, median about half a cent. Every model added here is CHEAPER per token than groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b, which the project has been running since 8 Sep. A full batch of 4 tasks x 7 models x 5 seeds is well under one dollar. Money was never the binding constraint, and BUDGET_USD_MAX exists to bound a runaway loop, not to ration.
openrouter._open_weight_check: ⚠️ Checked rather than assumed, because 'open-weight only' is a rule this project states and the provider API does not expose licences. Both additions of 9 Sep have official weight repositories from the originating organisation: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (apache-2.0, 6.7M downloads) and zai-org/GLM-5.3 (a custom licence, 474k downloads). The rule is about whether the weights exist outside an API, which both satisfy; it is not a claim that either licence permits redistribution, which this project never does.
openrouter._rejected_9_sep: ⚠️ Three model families were requested for the batch and NONE of them can be scored: every qwen3.8 variant, both glm-5.3 variants and moonshotai/kimi-k3 are in RED_TEAM (providers.mjs). They reviewed this project, and their critiques shaped the specification, the gates and the task corpus, so any score they earned would be contaminated by their own influence on the benchmark. They were priced and smoke-tested before that was checked, and resolve() refused them — which is the gate working as intended: its own comment warns that 'adding a price would have silently scored a reviewer', and adding a price is exactly what happened. The entries were removed rather than left inert.
openrouter._kimi_k3_second_reason: Independently of R14, kimi-k3 could not have run fairly at the current budget: at $3/$15 per M its worst-case round is $0.096, so $0.50 funds 5 rounds against a max_rounds of 8. It would have stopped two thirds of the way through while every other model ran to the declared limit, and the result would have read as the MODEL failing. Same defect as the $0.05 budget fixed on 9 Sep.
